digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler git write gate (check_raw_git_writes.py, rule R3)
propositions: R3 composition rule enforces that git-adapter mutation primitives (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) are called only from within the atomic-transaction seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py) or with a reasoned # raw-git-ok marker.

The existing checker (policy d37e, R1/R2) approved git_adapter primitive calls individually without enforcing the protocol rule that tracker mutations must compose atomically within a locked transaction, allowing reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 and __main__.py:338-351 to stage-and-commit outside the seam.

R3 detects seam-external calls via receiver binding (import-based and dynamic-loader-based git_adapter module references) without false positives on unrelated .add()/.commit() methods (set.add, session.commit).

Two out-of-transaction composition sites (reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot and __main__._purge_committed_reconciler_locks) receive durable reasoned inline markers explaining why they cannot route through the standard commit seam, blocking remediation debt.

The module-size gate required splitting __main__.py by extracting the pass-lock lifecycle cluster (_lock_steal_enabled, _resolve_held_lock, _purge_committed_reconciler_locks, _acquire_or_adopt_pass_lock) to _pass_lock_lifecycle.py, and R3 re-applied there to verify the rule's portability.

The sanctioned-entry set is keyed on exact repo-relative path, not filename alone, to prevent bypass via lookalike files in other packages; the receiver binding remains name-based because module name is evidence, not claim.
